look_here_first: Notice what is missing: there are no ray florets. Barbara's buttons makes a rounded button-like head of many tubular disc flowers. Then check the narrow leaves, hemispheric involucre, numerous paleae on the receptacle, and the persistent scale-like pappus on the cypselae.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: perennial herb with narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate leaves; heads discoid rather than radiate — no petal-like ray florets; showy rounded/button-like head containing many bisexual tubular florets; hemispheric involucre with several close series of narrow phyllaries; receptacle with conspicuous paleae/bractlets among flowers; five fused stamens per floret forming an anther cylinder; inferior ovary becoming a strongly ribbed cypsela; pappus of several persistent scales

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: Useful Asteraceae exception card: a showy composite head can be entirely disc florets and still be Asteraceae.

key_traits.label: Video training
key_traits.text: Joey's frame shows developing button-like capitula in local limestone habitat before full bloom.

lookalikes.differences: Use the large rounded button head, absence of ray florets, narrow leaves, involucre/paleae and pappus rather than flower color.
